title: Early-Stage Li Plating Dynamics Investigated by In Situ Liquid Phase Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Lithium metal is considered one of the most promising anode materials for next-generation batteries due to its extremely high theoretical capacity (3,860 mAh/g). However, the irregular electrodeposition of Li into dendrites remains a significant challenge causing serious safety risks, hindering the commercialization of Li metal batteries (LMBs). To address this, it is essential to understand the fundamental behaviors of Li growth, particularly during the initial nucleation phase.
